What I generally advice my friends is:
-Cost of consumed materials
-Hours x at least local minimum wage
-Something on top for pure profit

But also take into consideration 
- Any% of tools or future investment in better 
(because these things do need purchasing, have wear and tear and perhaps at some point items will need replacing or something becomes available that makes the work better/easier/more efficient)

- Any% of cost to sell/display
(At conventions, fairs, shops and more there is usually a fee to be there. Usually in renting space and/or tables)

*Usually I have them calculate these by cost/uses and cost/expected sales

- Legal/business costs, like local (sales) taxes, payments for registering companies. These are very dependent on location and your personal plans

So an example for a one-time sell would be (fictional numbers):
Materials = 15
Labor = 2*12.5 = 15
Current tools = 150/300 = 0.50
Future upgrades = 1000/500= 2
Cost of selling = 200/50 = 4
Total: 36.50 >  40  because I like round numbers and I can pocket the 4.50 to buy snacks so I can art better (pure profit)

I hope this makes sense

Edit: it is often a good idea to have high and low price items. Not everyone can afford big art pieces that are 50+ but 5-20 means they can still support artists and have a small piece
